The question

Can the shape of a new concept's first three years tell us how far it will travel?

Some scientific concepts stay in their home discipline; others cross into many fields within a few years. Simple popularity counts already explain much of that difference. The paper asks whether the structure of a concept's early adds anything beyond a five-feature popularity baseline, .

The answer

Yes, a little, and with the same sign everywhere it was measured. Concepts whose early home-field neighbourhood keeps picking up new, community-spanning topic partners later reach more fields than B5 predicts. The index has a pooled correlation with of

The effect is small. It is a descriptive pool, not a confirmation: five of the six bodies had their outcomes read in earlier analyses, and adding OPENhome to B5 gives no practical forecasting gain (+0.002 [−0.003, +0.008]).

      Try it

      Run the index yourself, and give the entry model more guesses

      Can I compute OPENhome myself?

      Live OPENhome calculator

      OPENhome is exact arithmetic: clip each component to its frozen bounds, z-score it with the frozen DEV mean and SD, flip the sign of ego density and edge persistence, and average the components that are defined. The calculator loads the concept selected in the browser; move a slider to see how the index responds. The percentile compares the result with all recorded OPENhome values.

      component counted as iscomponent with reversed sign (ego density, persistence)

      What if the model could name k candidate fields?

      Top-k hit rate of the entered field, R2 baseline versus R3

      What the paper does not show

      • Not a forecasting tool. OPENhome adds no forecasting gain over B5 (+0.002 [−0.003, +0.008]). The association is modest.
      • Not confirmatory for most bodies. Held-out outcomes were previously unsealed by two earlier experiments, so the indicator-screen held-out results are robustness checks. Only the 2015–17 cohort was never used before.
      • Not temporal churn. The within-concept permutation null absorbs the year-to-year component (excess NOVCHURN +0.008 [−0.02, +0.03] against raw +0.116 [+0.09, +0.14]). The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability of about 0.01–0.05, so temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted.
      • Not a within-concept mechanism. The closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields (−0.079 [−0.146, −0.013]).
      • Home-only signal is marginal. On the fresh cohort the DerSimonian–Laird pool includes zero (+0.083 [−0.007, +0.173]); about half of the OPENall signal is mechanical coupling with the outcome.
      • Retained frontier is PARTIAL. The volume-matched contrast is null, the coefficient reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity, and persistence and volume remain confounded.
      • Not causal. Early openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses.
      • Vocabulary bias. The legacy concept vocabulary is survivor-selected; the vocabulary-free Frame N is small (636 concepts) with pre-unseal power of 0.47.

      Where each view's data comes from

      • Headline forest: evaluation 4, results/evidence_synthesis.json (per-body PSP, CIs, placebo percentiles, DerSimonian–Laird pools).
      • Stepper, concept browser, fifths view, calculator, misses: experiment 16, full_method_out.json ( concepts; raw components, OPENhome, O2r m = 50, DEV-fitted forecasts); frozen OPEN constants from experiment 10, results/frozen_spec.json; GPU's early-entry counts from experiment 12, results/case_pairs.json.
      • Entry forest and robustness chart: experiment 7, results/frontier_result.json.
      • Entry browser and top-k view: experiment 7, full_method_out.json (252,922 held-out candidate rows; the top-k view uses the entered-field rank of every event, the browser a seeded sample of 30 risk sets per unit), with concept names from experiment 5, frame_concepts.csv.
      • Noise-control chart: experiment 16, results/clean_vs_raw_psp.json.

      Each dataset is embedded in this page as a JSON element whose data-source attribute names the artifact file; the charts are drawn from those elements.
